chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani, from Ali ibn Asbat and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of God the Exalted:
'So believe in God and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down'

He said: 'O Abu Khalid, the Light, by God, are the Imams (peace be upon them). O Abu Khalid, the light of the Imam in the hearts of the believers is more radiant than the bright sun by day. And they are those who illuminate the hearts of the believers. And God withholds their light from whomever He wills, so their hearts are darkened and they are covered by it.'

key_terms.النُّور: The Light — here interpreted as the Imam, a spiritual and metaphysical reality beyond physical light
key_terms.قُلُوبُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Hearts of the believers — the spiritual receptacle for the Imam's light
key_terms.يَحْجُبُ: Withholds/screens — God's act of depriving certain people of access to the Imam's light

ai.seo_question: What is 'the Light which We have sent down' in Quran 64:8 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records Abu Khalid al-Kabuli's inquiry to Imam al-Baqir (AS) about the Quranic phrase 'the Light which We have sent down' (64:8). The Imam identifies this Light emphatically — 'by God' — as the Imams themselves. He then elaborates: the Imam's light in the hearts of believers surpasses even the radiance of the midday sun, for the Imams are the source of spiritual illumination. Yet God withholds this light from whom He wills, leaving such people in spiritual darkness. This exegesis was profoundly significant to early Shia Muslims, establishing the Imams as the divinely-appointed intermediaries of spiritual guidance on earth.

en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Mahran has narrated from ‘Abd al-‘Azim ibn ‘Abdallah al-Hassani from Ali ibn Asbat and al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from abu Khalid al-kabuli who has said that
he asked Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the meaning of the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, in the following verse of the Holy Quran.
“Those who believe in him, honor and help him, and follow the light which is sent down to him, will have everlasting happiness.” [7:157]

The Imams (a.s.) said, “O abu Khalid, the light in this verse, I swear by Allah, means the Imams. O abu Khalid the light of the Imam (a.s.) in the hearts of the true believers is more bright than the light of the sun in midday. It is they who brighten the hearts of the true believers and Allah withholds their light from reaching whomever He would will, thus, their hearts become dark and Allah covers them with the darknesss.”
